title: Skydance’s Discovery+ prices increase by up to 20 percent
gist: Discovery+ raised prices to $12 ad-free and $7 ad-based a week after Paramount Skydance closed its purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, while Skydance plans to merge its streaming services into one over time.

themes.theme: Discovery+ price hike and Skydance consolidation

insights.claim: Discovery+ ad-free plans for new subscribers rose from $10 to $12 a month and ad-based from $6 to $7, with existing subscribers getting 30 days' notice and new prices starting with bills from November 12.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Continued streaming price hikes show pricing power in niche, low-churn services.

insights.claim: Skydance says the price increase was in the works before the merger close date was known and not planned in anticipation of the merger, though it came a week after Paramount Skydance bought Warner Bros. Discovery.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Timing invites skepticism, and further price moves are likely post-merger.

insights.claim: Discovery+ has been profitable since at least 2023 with low cancellation rates, and WBD's streaming CEO called it 'a tremendous opportunity' in February, but the last disclosed subscriber count was 24 million in 2022.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A profitable niche service gives Skydance a cash-generative asset, though disclosure is thin.
insights.locator: Discovery+ has been a smaller streaming venture

insights.claim: Skydance said it will combine its direct-to-consumer services, including Paramount+, Discovery+ and HBO Max, into a single service over time, which Ars notes could be expensive given Discovery+'s new price.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A bundled service may carry higher pricing and consolidate subscriber economics; watch for the combined tier's price.
insights.locator: We have yet to see what changes
